_comment: create-worktree config for quarterback itself. See worktrees/README.md for
the full key reference and worktrees/templates/ for copyable starting points.
Two choices here are deliberate and worth the note:
docker.enabled=false — docker-compose.yml is TRACKED in this repo, and the
Docker path writes its own compose file into the worktree. That would leave
every worktree permanently dirty and invite committing a generated compose.
Run a worktree's app directly instead: .venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app
--port $(cat .worktree-port). Postgres is shared from the main checkout's
compose stack; only the database inside it is per-worktree.
database.container=auto — the container is resolved by asking which running
Postgres answers as the URL's user, so this works whatever the checkout
directory (and therefore the compose project name) is called.
base_port starts at 5690 because the main compose stack already publishes
5681 for the app; allocating from 5681 hands a worktree a port it cannot bind.
Requires a .env in the main checkout (cp .env.example .env). That is the file
create-worktree copies and then repoints at the worktree's own database.
